result.rationale: In EventManager.ts the diff replaces the optional-chained `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` with `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` — no optional chaining on the destructured element. When destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (e.g. no calendar connected), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and `.integration` throws a TypeError, breaking the intended Cal Video fallback.

judged_text: The Meet-location fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without a null guard, crashing when destinationCalendar is null/empty (the old code used optional chaining). When evt.destinationCalendar is null (no calendar connected, the common single-user case) and location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws TypeError, failing the booking with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video as the contract promises.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The Meet-location fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without a null guard, crashing when destinationCalendar is null/empty (the old code used optional chaining). When evt.destinationCalendar is null (no calendar connected, the common single-user case) and location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws TypeError, failing the booking with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video as the contract promises.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new logic destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in the Meet fallback condition. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]` (which the diff shows is possible, e.g. `handleNewBooking` sets `destinationCalendar: ... : null`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` becomes `undefined` and `undefined.integration` will throw a TypeError. The prior code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) and would not crash, instead falling back as intended.
